title: Asteroids by Type
description: Asteroids sort by the light they reflect. C-types are dark and carbon-rich, with water locked in clays and organic molecules; S-types are stony and bright; M-types are metal, the cores of shattered small worlds, iron and nickel with the platinum-group metals. An asteroid's brightness alone does not give its size: a dark one must be bigger to look as bright. Unlocks C-type and M-type asteroid missions, found first with the Reflecting Telescope.

puzzle.goal: An asteroid of absolute magnitude H reflects a fraction p of the light that falls on it (its albedo). Write its diameter D in km, using 1329 km, the diameter of a body of H = 0 and p = 1.
puzzle.name: Size from brightness
puzzle.ask: Find D in km for H = @{H} and p = 0.05 (a C-type).
puzzle.method: Reflected light goes as p·D²; five magnitudes are a factor of a hundred in light, so D goes as 10^(−H/5)/√p.
